claim: At E9.5, bilateral nephrogenic cell populations expressing sine oculis-related homeobox 2 (Six2) were arranged as cords that lay medial to Wolffian ducts and lateral to the dorsal aorta in the caudal part of the mouse embryo.
source: At E9.5, bilateral nephrogenic cell populations, which expressed sine oculis-related homeobox 2 (Six2), were arranged as cords that lay medial to Wolffian ducts and lateral to the dorsal aorta in the caudal part of the mouse embryo (Figure 1a–c; Video 1).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1a-c and Video 1

claim: No F4/80+ macrophages were near to the Six2+ nephrogenic cords at E9.5.
source: No F4/80+ macrophages were near to the Six2+ nephrogenic cords at this stage (Figure 1c; Video 2).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1c and Video 2

claim: GFP-expressing cells arrived in the embryo-proper only from E9.5 onwards in Cx3cr1GFP embryos.
source: This finding is consistent with previous studies using Cx3cr1GFP embryos that showed GFP-expressing cells arrived in the embryo-proper only from E9.5 onwards (Mass et al., 2016; Gomez Perdiguero et al., 2013; Schulz et al., 2012; Stremmel et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: By E10.5, Six2+ metanephric cells had accumulated at the caudal end of the Wolffian duct as ureteric bud outgrowth started.
source: By E10.5, as ureteric bud outgrowth started, Six2+ metanephric cells had accumulated at the caudal end of the Wolffian duct (Figure 1d; Figure 1—figure supplement 1) (as previously described by Wainwright et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and citation to Wainwright et al., 2015

claim: The metanephric cell populations were avascular at E10.5.
source: Immunostaining for a pan-endothelial marker (CD31) demonstrated that the metanephric cell populations were avascular at this stage (Figure 1e; Video 2).
evidence: Supported by CD31 immunostaining data shown in Figure 1e and Video 2

claim: F4/80+ macrophages were present in high numbers in the caudal part of the E10.5 embryo.
source: F4/80+ macrophages were now present in high numbers in the caudal part of the embryo (Figure 1e–f).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1e-f

claim: F4/80+ macrophages largely avoided the metanephric mesenchyme at E10.5.
source: These macrophages largely avoided the metanephric mesenchyme (Figure 1e–f; Video 2) but localised in high numbers alongside rostral clusters of Six2+ cells (Figure 1g–h).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1e-f, Video 2, and Figure 1g-h

claim: F4/80+ macrophages localised in high numbers alongside rostral clusters of Six2+ cells at E10.5.
source: These macrophages largely avoided the metanephric mesenchyme (Figure 1e–f; Video 2) but localised in high numbers alongside rostral clusters of Six2+ cells (Figure 1g–h).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1g-h

claim: Six2+ nuclei of some rostral nephrogenic progenitors were observed within the cell bodies of macrophages.
source: Moreover, Six2+ nuclei of some rostral nephrogenic progenitors were observed within the cell bodies of macrophages, suggesting that active phagocytosis occurs at this site (Figure 1j; Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1j and Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: In all macrophage-depleted embryos, ureteric bud outgrowth had occurred only at the normal anatomical position.
source: In all macrophage-depleted embryos, ureteric bud outgrowth had occurred only at the normal anatomical position (in 9/9 kidneys analysed); however, its morphological development was delayed compared to littermate controls in E11.5 and E12.5 embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data from 9 kidneys shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: Ureteric bud morphological development was delayed in macrophage-depleted embryos compared to littermate controls in E11.5 and E12.5 embryos.
source: In all macrophage-depleted embryos, ureteric bud outgrowth had occurred only at the normal anatomical position (in 9/9 kidneys analysed); however, its morphological development was delayed compared to littermate controls in E11.5 and E12.5 embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: Vascular organisation appeared normal in macrophage-depleted embryos relative to the developmental stage of the kidney.
source: Vascular organisation appeared normal in macrophage-depleted embryos relative to the developmental stage of the kidney (Figure 1i; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1i and Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The ureteric bud had invaded the metanephric mesenchyme by E11 and bifurcated by E11.5.
source: The ureteric bud had invaded the metanephric mesenchyme by E11 and bifurcated by E11.5 (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2a-b

claim: At E11-E11.5, numerous F4/80+ macrophages and blood vessels were present in the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme.
source: At E11-E11.5, numerous F4/80+ macrophages and blood vessels were present in the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme (situated between the metanephric mesenchyme and Wolffian duct), but relatively few were present within the metanephric mesenchyme (Figure 2a–c).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2a-c

claim: At E11-E11.5, relatively few F4/80+ macrophages and blood vessels were present within the metanephric mesenchyme.
source: At E11-E11.5, numerous F4/80+ macrophages and blood vessels were present in the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme (situated between the metanephric mesenchyme and Wolffian duct), but relatively few were present within the metanephric mesenchyme (Figure 2a–c).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2a-c

claim: Macrophage density was higher in the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme than the metanephric mesenchyme at E11.5.
source: Macrophage density is higher in the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme than the metanephric mesenchyme (macrophage density in peri-Wolffian mesenchyme (PWM) = 260.20 ± 20.08 per mm2 [mean ±SEM]; macrophage density in metanephric mesenchyme (MM) = 95.86 ± 12.29 per mm2 [mean ±SEM]; two-tailed paired t-test [testing whether densities were the same]; p<0.0001; n = 10 kidneys from five embryos).
evidence: Supported by quantification data from 10 kidneys shown in Figure 2c

claim: Up until E12.5, kidney macrophages are yolk sac-derived.
source: Up until E12.5, kidney macrophages are yolk sac-derived (Hoeffel et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hoeffel et al., 2015

claim: F4/80+ macrophages within the E11-E11.5 peri-Wolffian mesenchyme were always extravascular.
source: Whole-mount immunostaining demonstrated that F4/80+ macrophages within the E11-E11.5 peri-Wolffian mesenchyme were always extravascular (Figure 2a–b), which led us to hypothesise that these macrophages travel via trans-tissue migration.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2a-b

claim: Time-lapse imaging of cultured E11.5 Csf1rEGFP kidneys indicated that macrophages migrate via extravascular routes.
source: Indeed, time-lapse imaging of cultured E11.5 Csf1rEGFP kidneys indicated that these macrophages migrate via extravascular routes and regularly interact with other macrophages as well as the abluminal surfaces of isolectin B4-labelled blood vessels (Video 3).
evidence: Supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Video 3

claim: Blood vessels begin entering the kidney from the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme between E11.5-E12 when interstitial tissue regions first form.
source: Blood vessels begin entering the kidney from the peri-Wolffian mesenchyme between E11.5-E12 when interstitial tissue regions first form (Munro et al., 2017b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Munro et al., 2017b

claim: At E11.5, Six2+ nephron progenitor cells were present throughout the metanephric mesenchyme as a single population, which contained very few macrophages.
source: At E11.5, Six2+ nephron progenitor cells were present throughout the metanephric mesenchyme as a single population, which contained very few macrophages (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2d

claim: By E12.5, the Six2+ population had split.
source: By E12.5, the Six2+ population had split (Figure 2e), resulting in the 'capping' of each ureteric bud tip (Herring, 1900; Short et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2e and citations to Herring, 1900 and Short et al., 2014

claim: F4/80+ macrophages had occupied interstitial fissures by E12.5 and commonly wrapped around the interstitial blood vessels.
source: Whole-mount imaging of E12.5 kidneys demonstrated that F4/80+ macrophages had occupied these interstitial fissures and commonly wrapped around the interstitial blood vessels (Figure 2e–f).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2e-f

claim: All detectable F4/80+ cells co-expressed Csf1r at E14.5.
source: At E14.5, all detectable F4/80+ cells co-expressed Csf1r (100 ± 0%, mean ±SEM) (Figure 3a; Video 4).
evidence: Supported by co-immunostaining data shown in Figure 3a and Video 4

claim: F4/80, CD31, and Gata3 co-staining demonstrated that macrophages were present throughout the medullary and cortical portions of developing kidneys and were often localised around the renal vasculature.
source: F4/80, CD31, and Gata3 co-staining demonstrated that macrophages were present throughout the medullary and cortical portions of developing kidneys and were often localised around the renal vasculature (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Video 5).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Video 5

claim: Macrophages often arranged parallel to major renal blood vessels, such as segmental arteries, but did not typically interact with their endothelial cells.
source: Macrophages often arranged parallel to major renal blood vessels, such as segmental arteries, but did not typically interact with their endothelial cells (Figure 3b; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Macrophages directly interacted with endothelium of small calibre vessels, such as the newly forming cortical nephrogenic zone blood vessels.
source: In contrast, macrophages directly interacted with endothelium of small calibre vessels, such as the newly forming cortical nephrogenic zone blood vessels (Figure 3c–d).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3c-d

claim: 89.6 ± 1.45% (mean ±SEM) of macrophages localised within the interstitium in the E17.5 peripheral nephrogenic zone.
source: Using the E17.5 peripheral nephrogenic zone as a representative example, we determined that 89.6 ± 1.45% (mean ±SEM) of macrophages localised within the interstitium, the remainder being within the cap mesenchyme (nephron progenitor populations; Figure 3e; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: Of the interstitial macrophages in the E17.5 peripheral nephrogenic zone, 78.5 ± 2.1% (mean ±SEM) were in contact with the abluminal surface of blood vessels.
source: Of the interstitial macrophages, 78.5 ± 2.1% (mean ±SEM) were in contact with the abluminal surface of blood vessels, and we defined these cells as perivascular macrophages (Figure 3e; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3e and Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: The alignment of perivascular macrophages strongly correlated with the alignment of their associated blood vessel.
source: The alignment of perivascular macrophages, which we defined based on their longest axis, strongly correlated with the alignment of their associated blood vessel (Figure 3f).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3f

claim: No entirely intravascular F4/80high kidney macrophages were detected.
source: We did not detect any entirely intravascular F4/80high kidney macrophages, indicating that these cells either arrived via extravascular routes, that precursor cells gained F4/80high status only after exiting the vasculature, or a combination thereof.
evidence: Based on observations from immunostaining data

claim: Most macrophages in the cortical nephrogenic zone never expressed the renal interstitial cell markers Meis1/2.
source: Although most macrophages were interstitial, they never expressed the renal cortical interstitial markers Meis1/2 (Brunskill et al., 2008) (Figure 3h), consistent with the documented exogenous origins of kidney macrophages (Hoeffel et al., 2015; Kobayashi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3h and citations to Brunskill et al., 2008, Hoeffel et al., 2015, and Kobayashi et al., 2014

claim: Within the cortical nephrogenic zone, F4/80high macrophages typically co-stained for the mannose receptor, CD206.
source: Within the cortical nephrogenic zone, F4/80high macrophages typically co-stained for the mannose receptor, CD206, a marker associated with perivascular/mature macrophage status (Figure 3i–j) (Faraco et al., 2016; Galea et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3i-j and citations to Faraco et al., 2016 and Galea et al., 2005

claim: At E11.5, before the nephrogenic zone formed, F4/80+ macrophages typically co-expressed CD206.
source: Even at E11.5, before the nephrogenic zone formed, F4/80+ macrophages typically co-expressed CD206 (Figure 3i).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3i

claim: CD206 predominantly localised in intracellular vesicle membranes, while F4/80 localised in the plasma membrane.
source: Immunostaining confirmed that CD206+ macrophages were often perivascular (Figure 3—figure supplement 4) and demonstrated that CD206 predominantly localised in intracellular vesicle membranes, while F4/80 localised in the plasma membrane (most highly at sites of lamellipodia and filopodia) (Figure 3k–k').
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4 and Figure 3k-k'

claim: Macrophages were observed in contact with the basement membrane of developing nephrons.
source: In accordance with this finding, we observed macrophages in contact with the basement membrane of developing nephrons (Figure 3—figure supplement 5; Video 6).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and Video 6

claim: Macrophages frequently interacted with blood vessels that wrapped around the developing nephron tubules.
source: Macrophages also frequently interacted with blood vessels that wrapped around the developing nephron tubules (Figure 3—figure supplement 5; Video 6).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and Video 6

claim: Gal3+ cells were largely distinct from CD206+ macrophages, although a small percentage of cells co-expressed both proteins.
source: Gal3+ cells were largely distinct from CD206+ macrophages, although a small percentage of cells co-expressed both proteins (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4b-d

claim: The proportion of myeloid cells that were Gal3+ increased substantially later in development, while the relative proportion of CD206+ cells decreased.
source: The proportion of myeloid cells that were Gal3+ increased substantially later in development, while the relative proportion of CD206+ cells decreased (Figure 4d; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4d and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: At E17.5, 14.4% ± 2.2% (mean ±SEM) of Gal3+ myeloid cells in the cortical nephrogenic zone were being carried within blood vessels at the point of fixation.
source: At E17.5, 14.4% ± 2.2% (mean ±SEM) of Gal3+ myeloid cells in the cortical nephrogenic zone were being carried within blood vessels at the point of fixation (Figure 4e–f'; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4e-f' and Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: Gal3+ cells were morphologically spherical in comparison to the irregular morphology of the CD206+ macrophages.
source: Gal3+ cells were morphologically spherical in comparison to the irregular morphology of the CD206+ macrophages (Figure 4g).
evidence: Supported by morphological quantification data shown in Figure 4g

claim: Distinct clusters of F4/80highCD206highGal3low and Gal3highF4/80lowCD206low macrophages were identified by PCA.
source: By performing PCA specifically on these macrophages, distinct clusters of F4/80highCD206highGal3low and Gal3highF4/80lowCD206low macrophage were identified (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), substantiating our immunofluorescence observations.
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3

claim: The mRNA signatures of F4/80highCD206high cells, but not of Gal3high cells, were consistent with their being mature macrophages.
source: The mRNA signatures of F4/80highCD206high cells, but not of Gal3high cells, were consistent with their being mature macrophages (signatures based on Mass et al., 2016) (Figure 4h–i).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4h-i and citation to Mass et al., 2016

claim: Genes associated with immune response were enriched in the top 1% of genes expressed by Gal3high cells.
source: PANTHER gene over-representation testing (http://www.pantherdb.org/) demonstrated that genes associated with biological processes such as immune response (false discovery rate [FDR] corrected p=1.22×10−4) and defence response (FDR corrected p=1.25×10−4) were enriched in the top 1% of genes expressed by Gal3high cells (Figure 4j; Supplementary file 2), suggesting that Gal3high macrophages are primed for pathogenic invasion.
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data shown in Figure 4j and Supplementary file 2

claim: The top 1% of genes expressed by F4/80highCD206high cells were over-represented in biological processes such as pinocytosis, endocytosis, endosomal transport, and phagocytosis.
source: The top 1% of genes expressed by F4/80highCD206high cells were over-represented in biological processes such as pinocytosis (FDR corrected p=3.8×10−3), endocytosis (FDR corrected p=1.6×10−8), endosomal transport (FDR corrected p=2.1×10−3), and phagocytosis (FDR corrected p=1×10−2) (Figure 4k; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data shown in Figure 4k and Supplementary file 3

claim: Biological processes relating to tissue development were enriched in the F4/80highCD206high macrophages.
source: Notably, biological processes relating to tissue development were also enriched in the F4/80highCD206high macrophages (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data in Supplementary file 3

claim: Biological processes relating to vascularisation, such as vasculature development and blood vessel morphogenesis, were enriched in F4/80highCD206high macrophages.
source: Of these processes, several related to vascularisation, such as vasculature development (FDR corrected p=2.7×10−2) and blood vessel morphogenesis (FDR corrected p=3.9×10−2).
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data

claim: Gene expression by Gal3high cells was not associated with development-related processes.
source: Gene expression by Gal3high cells was not associated with development-related processes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data in Supplementary file 2

claim: CD206 (MRC1 in the human) and Gal3 (LGALS3 in the human) were differentially expressed in immune cell types of the human embryonic kidney.
source: In agreement with our results in the mouse, CD206 (MRC1 in the human) and Gal3 (LGALS3 in the human) were differentially expressed in immune cell types of the human embryonic kidney (Figure 5a–i).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human kidney shown in Figure 5a-i

claim: 90% of MRC1+ cells were macrophages (group 11) in the developing human kidney.
source: 90% of MRC1+ cells were macrophages (group 11) (Figure 5h), whereas LGALS3+ immune cells were distributed between the macrophage cluster (group 11; 58% of LGALS3+ immune cells) and a distinct leukocyte cluster (group 10; 42% of LGALS3+ immune cells) (Figure 5i).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human kidney shown in Figure 5h

claim: LGALS3+ immune cells were distributed between the macrophage cluster (group 11; 58% of LGALS3+ immune cells) and a distinct leukocyte cluster (group 10; 42% of LGALS3+ immune cells) in the developing human kidney.
source: 90% of MRC1+ cells were macrophages (group 11) (Figure 5h), whereas LGALS3+ immune cells were distributed between the macrophage cluster (group 11; 58% of LGALS3+ immune cells) and a distinct leukocyte cluster (group 10; 42% of LGALS3+ immune cells) (Figure 5i).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human kidney shown in Figure 5i

claim: The group 10 immune cells specifically expressed L-selectin (SELL) in the developing human kidney.
source: The group 10 immune cells specifically expressed L-selectin (SELL) (Figure 5g), which functions to tether leukocytes to endothelium (Stein et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human kidney shown in Figure 5g and citation to Stein et al., 1999

claim: F4/80 (EMR1 in the human) was not expressed by macrophages in the foetal human kidney.
source: F4/80 (EMR1 in the human) was not expressed by macrophages in the foetal human kidney (Figure 5j), consistent with a previous report showing EMR1 is not expressed by human macrophages (Hamann et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data from human kidney shown in Figure 5j and citation to Hamann et al., 2007

claim: Vascular density was markedly reduced in kidneys treated with pan-VEGF inhibitors (sunitinib, vatalanib, and semaxanib).
source: Vascular density was markedly reduced in the treated kidneys (Figure 6a–c), but macrophage localisation (in/out of the interstitium) did not differ between groups (one-way ANOVA; p=0.7142; n = 4–9 kidneys per group) (Figure 6d).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6a-c

claim: Macrophage localisation (in/out of the interstitium) did not differ between control and vascular-depleted kidney groups.
source: Vascular density was markedly reduced in the treated kidneys (Figure 6a–c), but macrophage localisation (in/out of the interstitium) did not differ between groups (one-way ANOVA; p=0.7142; n = 4–9 kidneys per group) (Figure 6d).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6d

claim: Macrophage density was reduced in vascular-depleted kidneys.
source: Notably, macrophage density was reduced in vascular-depleted kidneys (Figure 6e) and was positively correlated with vascular density when assessing all groups (r = 0.71; p<0.0001) (Figure 6f) and even when assessing only control groups (r = 0.74; p=0.004) (Figure 6g).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6e

claim: Macrophage density was positively correlated with vascular density when assessing all groups (r = 0.71; p<0.0001).
source: Notably, macrophage density was reduced in vascular-depleted kidneys (Figure 6e) and was positively correlated with vascular density when assessing all groups (r = 0.71; p<0.0001) (Figure 6f) and even when assessing only control groups (r = 0.74; p=0.004) (Figure 6g).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6f

claim: Macrophage density was positively correlated with vascular density when assessing only control groups (r = 0.74; p=0.004).
source: Notably, macrophage density was reduced in vascular-depleted kidneys (Figure 6e) and was positively correlated with vascular density when assessing all groups (r = 0.71; p<0.0001) (Figure 6f) and even when assessing only control groups (r = 0.74; p=0.004) (Figure 6g).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6g

claim: F4/80+ macrophages engulf erythrocytes in the developing kidney.
source: We observed F4/80+ macrophages engulfing erythrocytes and dying endothelial cells in the kidney (Figure 7a–b; Video 7), demonstrating that, as well as spatially associating with the vasculature, kidney macrophages directly interact with blood and vascular components during development.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7a-b and Video 7

claim: F4/80+ macrophages engulf dying endothelial cells in the developing kidney.
source: We observed F4/80+ macrophages engulfing erythrocytes and dying endothelial cells in the kidney (Figure 7a–b; Video 7), demonstrating that, as well as spatially associating with the vasculature, kidney macrophages directly interact with blood and vascular components during development.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7a-b and Video 7

claim: Genes associated with vascular development are significantly over-represented in the top 1% of expressed genes in F4/80highCD206high macrophages.
source: Genes associated with vascular development are significantly over-represented in the top 1% of expressed genes in F4/80highCD206high macrophages, but not in the top 1% of the Gal3high myeloid cells.
evidence: Supported by gene over-representation testing data shown in Figure 7c-d

claim: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had fewer macrophages relative to control treated kidneys.
source: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had (g) fewer macrophages (p<0.0001), (h) reduced kidney area (p=0.0046), (j) more isolated endothelial structures (p=0.011), and (k) smaller endothelial structures (p=0.046) relative to control treated kidneys (n = 5 biological replicates; 1 field of view per kidney).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7g

claim: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had reduced kidney area relative to control treated kidneys.
source: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had (g) fewer macrophages (p<0.0001), (h) reduced kidney area (p=0.0046), (j) more isolated endothelial structures (p=0.011), and (k) smaller endothelial structures (p=0.046) relative to control treated kidneys (n = 5 biological replicates; 1 field of view per kidney).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7h

claim: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had more isolated endothelial structures relative to control treated kidneys.
source: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had (g) fewer macrophages (p<0.0001), (h) reduced kidney area (p=0.0046), (j) more isolated endothelial structures (p=0.011), and (k) smaller endothelial structures (p=0.046) relative to control treated kidneys (n = 5 biological replicates; 1 field of view per kidney).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7j

claim: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had smaller endothelial structures relative to control treated kidneys.
source: Anti-Csf1r treated kidneys had (g) fewer macrophages (p<0.0001), (h) reduced kidney area (p=0.0046), (j) more isolated endothelial structures (p=0.011), and (k) smaller endothelial structures (p=0.046) relative to control treated kidneys (n = 5 biological replicates; 1 field of view per kidney).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7k

claim: Vascular density (CD31+ area per field) did not significantly differ between anti-Csf1r treated and control treated kidneys.
source: (i) Vascular density (CD31+ area per field) did not significantly differ between groups (p=0.077).
evidence: Supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7i

claim: Macrophages support production and/or maintenance of endothelial cross-connections in the developing kidney.
source: These data demonstrate that macrophages support production and/or maintenance of endothelial cross-connections in the developing kidney.
evidence: Based on experimental data showing more isolated endothelial structures in macrophage-depleted kidneys

claim: Kidneys depleted of macrophages contained discontinuous endothelial structures, while control-treated kidneys had characteristic net-like vascular plexuses.
source: Kidneys depleted of macrophages contained discontinuous endothelial structures, while control-treated kidneys had characteristic net-like vascular plexuses.
evidence: Based on experimental data from macrophage depletion experiments

claim: Macrophages have the capacity to promote vascular anastomoses.
source: These data are consistent with macrophages having the capacity to promote vascular anastomoses, as has been described in other biological settings (Fantin et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: Based on experimental data and citations to Fantin et al., 2010 and Liu et al., 2016

claim: Lineage tracing studies in mice suggest that kidney macrophages are initially derived from the yolk sac but are derived almost exclusively from foetal monocytes after birth.
source: Lineage tracing studies in mice suggest that kidney macrophages are initially derived from the yolk sac but are derived almost exclusively from foetal monocytes after birth (Epelman et al., 2014; Hoeffel et al., 2015; Munro and Hughes, 2017; Sheng et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Epelman et al., 2014, Hoeffel et al., 2015, Munro and Hughes, 2017, and Sheng et al., 2015

claim: In the adult kidney, perivascular macrophages survey vascular transport for small immune complexes.
source: In the adult, macrophages and endothelial cells form anatomical and functional units that function to clear immune complexes from the renal blood (Stamatiades et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Stamatiades et al., 2016

claim: Kidney development begins when the caudal Wolffian duct is induced to branch, forming a ureteric bud that invades the metanephric mesenchyme by embryonic day (E) 11 in the mouse.
source: Kidney development begins when the caudal Wolffian duct is induced to branch, forming a ureteric bud that invades the metanephric mesenchyme by embryonic day (E) 11 in the mouse (Pichel et al., 1996; Saxén and Sariola, 1987).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pichel et al., 1996 and Saxén and Sariola, 1987

claim: The ureteric bud undergoes rounds of iterative branching to form the adult collecting duct tree.
source: The ureteric bud undergoes rounds of iterative branching to form the adult collecting duct tree, while cells endogenous to the metanephric mesenchyme generate nephrons and stroma (Grobstein, 1955; Kobayashi et al., 2008; Epelman et al., 2014; Shakya et al., 2005; Short et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Grobstein, 1955, Kobayashi et al., 2008, Epelman et al., 2014, Shakya et al., 2005, and Short et al., 2014

claim: Cells endogenous to the metanephric mesenchyme generate nephrons and stroma.
source: The ureteric bud undergoes rounds of iterative branching to form the adult collecting duct tree, while cells endogenous to the metanephric mesenchyme generate nephrons and stroma (Grobstein, 1955; Kobayashi et al., 2008; Epelman et al., 2014; Shakya et al., 2005; Short et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Grobstein, 1955, Kobayashi et al., 2008, Epelman et al., 2014, Shakya et al., 2005, and Short et al., 2014

claim: Monocytes, macrophages, and most endothelial cells in the kidney derive from extra-renal sources.
source: Other kidney cell types, such as monocytes, macrophages, and most endothelial cells, derive from extra-renal sources (Epelman et al., 2014; Hoeffel et al., 2015; DeFalco et al., 2014; Sequeira-Lopez et al., 2015; Sims-Lucas et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Epelman et al., 2014, Hoeffel et al., 2015, DeFalco et al., 2014, Sequeira-Lopez et al., 2015, and Sims-Lucas et al., 2013

claim: At E9.5-E10.5, all macrophages in the embryo-proper are derived from the yolk sac and express colony-stimulating factor one receptor (Csf1r), fractalkine receptor (Cx3cr1), and EGF-like module receptor 1 (F4/80).
source: At these stages, all macrophages in the embryo-proper are derived from the yolk sac and express colony-stimulating factor one receptor (Csf1r), fractalkine receptor (Cx3cr1), and EGF-like module receptor 1 (F4/80) (Mass et al., 2016; Schulz et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mass et al., 2016 and Schulz et al., 2012

claim: Csf1r and Cx3cr1 mark both mature macrophages and their precursors, whereas F4/80 marks only mature macrophages.
